annotator_problems: Pitch 1: the earliest live pre-motion frame after the cutaway is 3731.00, and Megill is already planted on the rubber with Albies in the box there, but the scoreboard bug goes fully white (a blank white box) at 3732.25 and 3732.50 and is still only half-drawn at 3733.00 and 3733.25 while the graphic wipes from the line-score box back to the normal bug. Per the continuity rule that wipe breaks the window, so the decision was taken as the first fully valid frame after the last break (3733.50) rather than 3731.00. If the wipe were treated as a readability-partial rather than a break, the decision for pitch 1 would instead be 3730.75-3731.00.

Pitch 1 judgement call: at the reported decision frame 3733.50 the bug's score, runners, outs, inning and count are all fully drawn and readable, but the pitcher line still reads 'MEGILL P:7' with the last pitch-count digit mid-render; 'P:75' is clean at 3733.75 and 3734.00. I marked readability 'readable' because the scoreboard fields the convention names are all legible, but a stricter reading of condition (4) would move pitch 1's decision to 3733.75.

Pitch 3 release is not a sampled frame: 3768.10 shows the arm over the top and extended with the hand motion-blurred and no ball yet separated, while 3768.20 already has the ball well in flight, so 3768.15 is the midpoint of that 0.10 s bracket. Pitch 1's release at 3735.80 is a sampled frame but the ball is only just clear of the hand, so the true release could be a frame or two earlier. Both are covered by the stated 0.15 s uncertainty.

The batter line ('2.ALBIES 1-1') is not shown on the bug at the pitch 1 and pitch 2 decision frames (3733.50 and 3746.50); it is present from 3748.25 onward and at every pitch 3 and pitch 4 frame. Batter identity for pitches 1 and 2 therefore rests on the nearby banner plus the full-screen '2B OZZIE ALBIES' graphic seen at 3726.00-3730.75.

The pitch clock on the bug is visibly inconsistent (e.g. :09 at both 3746.25 and 3746.50, :03 held across 3765.75-3768.30, :04 across 3782.00-3785.60), confirming it freezes and lags; it was recorded only as part of the raw bug text and not used for timing.

No discrepancy against the expected PA state: every readable frame in 3733.50-3785.60 shows NYM 0 / ATL 2, bases empty, 0 outs and a down-arrow 5, with counts 0-0 / 1-0 / 2-0 / 3-0 and P:75 / P:76 / P:77 / P:78 in order, matching the four expected pitches.

annotator_problems: Anchor disagreement: the session scan supplied with the task says '3960 no bug', but at 3960.00 I read a fully readable bug (NYM 0 / ATL 2, bases empty, down-5, 2 outs, 0-1, MEGILL :07 P:85, 4. OLSON 1-2). I used what I read. Frames 3955.00-3959.75 are a live overhead wide shot that does carry the bug too, so I saw no bug-less stretch anywhere between 3955 and 3968.

At the pitch-1 decision frame (3939.75) the bug's second banner line (the batter) is not displayed; it first appears at 3941.25 as '4. OLSON 1-2'. Batter identity at 3939.75 therefore rests on the immediately preceding close-up graphic ('1B MATT OLSON / 1 FOR 2 SINGLE', 3935.00-3939.50) and on the left-handed batter visible in the box, not on the bug itself.

The pitch-2 pre-decision shot (3955.00, 3958.00-3959.75) is a live high overhead scenic wide angle, not a replay or a dugout cutaway. I recorded failing_condition_before as 'cutaway_or_replay' because at that distance neither the pitcher's contact with the rubber (he is standing in front of it) nor the batter being in the box can be resolved, i.e. it is not an angle that 'clearly shows the pitcher on the rubber AND the batter'; a stricter reading could equally call it a condition-(2) failure. If that wide angle were accepted as qualifying, the pitch-2 decision would move earlier than 3960.00.

Release timing is bracketed at 0.05 s but is still a manual judgement. Pitch 1: 3945.35 shows the forearm over the top with the hand still above the head and 3945.40 shows the arm extended forward with the hand empty, so release could be one 0.05 s step either side of 3945.40. Pitch 2: 3966.95 shows the hand still cocked above the head, 3967.00 shows the arm extended forward and 3967.05 shows the extension with the hand clearly empty; I took 3967.00, but 3967.05 is equally defensible. Both are covered by the stated 0.15 s uncertainty.

The bug shows '81 MPH' at 3968.00 while the ball from the 3967.00 release was still in flight toward the plate, i.e. the speed readout came up faster than the stated 2-3 s bug lag would suggest. Reported only as a reading; it was not used for any timing.

Remote MP4 reads were extremely slow throughout (other concurrent PA units were reading the same file), roughly one frame every 1-2 minutes, so the frame budget was kept tight. Times reported at 0.05 s granularity should still be treated as manual, not frame-exact.

Pitch 1's continuity window has a maximum sample gap of 0.75 s and pitch 2's is exactly 1.00 s, both within the 1.0 s rule but coarse enough that a very brief (<1 s) graphic wipe between samples could have gone unseen.
